key_insight: The paper reframes safety for meta-RL in an information space that includes both physical state and task belief, enabling a learnable safety probability for adaptation.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to make adaptive RL safer in uncertain real-world settings by filtering unsafe actions and constraining policy updates during task adaptation.
method: Define safety in information space rather than state space alone.
Introduce a safety value function for the probability of avoiding unsafe regions indefinitely.
Derive self-consistency and Bellman equations to learn the safety value with meta-RL, then use it for safety filtering and constrained policy optimization.
evidence_signal: The proposed method is evaluated on meta-RL benchmarks, where it is reported to be effective.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurately learning belief-aware safety values, which may be sensitive to modeling assumptions and the quality of uncertainty estimates during adaptation.
paper_title: Safe Meta-Reinforcement Learning via Information Space Reachability
